title: DFT+U+V is equivalent to DFT+U with density-dependent hybridized projectors
authors: Edward Linscott, Alberto Carta, Nicola Marzari
abstract: Hubbard-corrected density-functional theory (DFT+$U$) is a popular tool for first-principles modeling of materials with localized $d$ or $f$ electrons, but its on-site corrections tend to over-localize charge and break covalent bonds. Inter-site $+V$ corrections were introduced to counter this and are now widely used, but a formal justification has been lacking. Here we show that -- to first order in $V/U$ -- inter-site corrections are exactly equivalent to on-site DFT+$U$ evaluated on a density-dependent redefinition of the Hubbard projectors, hybridized with those of neighboring sites, providing insight into the explicit mechanism by which $V$ affects covalency. If the projectors are held frozen, as is common practice, the equivalence partially breaks down. Beyond reinterpreting the formalism, these results sharpen the questions of how $V$ should be computed and what the Hubbard subspaces fundamentally are.
summary: This work mathematically proves that the inter-site $+V$ correction in $	ext{DFT}+U+V$ can be understood as an effective modification of the on-site Hubbard interaction ($+U$). This equivalence holds when using density-dependent, hybridized projectors, providing crucial physical insight into how electron correlation and covalency interact in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The authors aim to provide a formal justification for inter-site $+V$ corrections added to DFT+$U$, which are necessary because standard $	ext{DFT}+U$ over-localizes charge and breaks covalent bonds.
main_result: To first order in $V/U$, the full $	ext{DFT}+U+V$ potential is shown to be exactly equivalent to an on-site $	ext{DFT}+U$ calculation performed using density-dependent, hybridized Hubbard projectors.
method: The equivalence is demonstrated by defining a specific anti-Hermitian generator ($\hat{S}$) that relates the energy calculated with hybridized projectors to the full $	ext{DFT}+U+V$ energy in a perturbative expansion.
model_or_system: The study applies to materials containing localized $d$ or $f$ electrons, such as transition metal oxides (e.g., NiO). The theoretical framework involves extending standard DFT+$U$ with an inter-site potential term ($\hat{V}$).
key_observables: Potential matrix elements comparing $	ext{DFT}+U+V$ to approximations using hybridized projectors; the degree of covalency enhancement.
important_parameters: $U$ (Hubbard parameter), $V$ (inter-site correction strength); the perturbative limit $V/U \ll 1$.
main_assumptions: The equivalence is rigorously proven only to first order in $V/U$; using frozen projectors, a common practice, causes the formal equivalence to break down.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the evolution of Hubbard projectors (original vs. hybridized) for NiO, showing how hybridization incorporates neighboring orbital weights. Other figures compare potential matrix elements across different approximations and k-points.
paper_structure: The paper develops the equivalence by first establishing the formal relationship using a continuous parameter $\alpha$, then demonstrating that frozen projector approaches fail to reproduce the full potential, ultimately confirming the validity of the hybridized projector approach to first order in $V/U$.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, understanding how an effective Hamiltonian (like DFT+$U$) can be rigorously mapped onto a more complex correlated model ($	ext{DFT}+U+V$) using projection techniques is highly relevant for developing accurate many-body Hamiltonians in quantum simulation.
